title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 164 (Disqualifications for appointment of director)

content.overview: Section 164 lists personal disqualifications and the additional disqualification of directors of a company that defaults in filings or repayment.
content.glance: Section 164 lists personal disqualifications and the additional disqualification of directors of a company that defaults in filings or repayment.
content.study: Personal bars include unsoundness of mind declared by a court, undischarged insolvency, pending application to be adjudicated insolvent, conviction and sentence of at least six months with a five-year bar from expiry (and a five-year extension of the bar where the sentence is seven years or more), a court order disqualifying the person, unpaid calls, and conviction of a related-party offence under s. 188. Subsection (2) disqualifies a person who is or was a director of a company which has not filed financial statements or annual returns for three continuous financial years, or has failed to repay deposits, redeem debentures, or pay a declared dividend for one year or more. The person remains disqualified for five years. Private-company articles may add grounds. The ROC list under the related rules is evidence of the filing default, but the statutory test is the section.

examples.title: Three-year non-filing
examples.body: Directors of a company that misses financial statements or annual returns for three continuous years incur the five-year disqualification.

examples.title: Conviction
examples.body: A sentence of six months or more triggers the conviction bar from the date the sentence expires.

hypotheticals.facts: Directors of a company that misses financial statements or annual returns for three continuous years incur the five-year disqualification.

distinctions: Section 164 is disqualification to be appointed or to continue. Section 167 is vacation of office, and it picks up s. 164(2) in the circumstances stated there.

misconceptions.correction: Section 164 lists personal disqualifications and the additional disqualification of directors of a company that defaults in filings or repayment.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Does a filing default disqualify only the managing director?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. Section 164(2) covers a person who is or was a director of the defaulting company.
